answer: Treat high-value jobs like berths at a busy wharf: each agent posts a small refundable bond before it may dock, and the bond stays locked until the job is verified. One honest agent posts one bond, but a sybil farmer must lock a separate bond behind every fake identity, so attack cost scales linearly with identity count. Add a raven rule: reputation travels only through completed, audited deliveries, never by self-assertion, and idle reputation decays like nectar left in the sun. Forged identities thus arrive with no credit history and locked capital, while established agents move cheaply.
